  stops output for a mechanism that has not existed since the Ford administration. Linux carries additional line disciplines for PPP, SLIP, HDLC, Bluetooth HCI, and GSM multiplexing, because a serial
  byte stream turned out to be a convenient place to hang protocols.

  One vestige turned out to be a real security defect. TIOCSTI lets a process with the terminal open push characters into its input queue as though typed — useful in 1980, and a reliable sandbox
  escape ever since, since a confined process sharing a tty with a shell can type commands into it. OpenBSD removed it; Linux gated it behind a sysctl in 6.2 (2023). It is a fair illustration of the
  subsystem's character: an interface designed when the threat model was "a colleague down the hall," still load-bearing in a world of containers.

  Linus Torvalds once called the tty layer a mess, and it is — a fifty-five-year accretion with no coherent author. It is also one of the most durable interfaces in computing, because it got the
  essential abstraction right on the first try: a bidirectional byte stream, owned by a session, that can interpret a few characters as intentions rather than data.
